#!/bin/bash
# Usage: set-wallpaper.sh /path/to/image-or-video [transition]
# Applies the wallpaper to every monitor Yin knows about.

WALLPAPER="$1"
TRANSITION="$2"   # optional, e.g. zoom / bookflip (see `yinctl --list-trans`)
[ -z "$WALLPAPER" ] && { echo "Usage: $0 <path> [transition]"; exit 1; }

# Build the optional --trans flag only when a transition was given.
trans_args=()
[ -n "$TRANSITION" ] && trans_args=(--trans "$TRANSITION")

# Discover monitors from yin's per-monitor state files in ~/.cache/yin.
# Cached media is named "<W>x<H>_<file>"; anything else is a monitor name.
monitors=$(ls ~/.cache/yin 2>/dev/null | grep -vE '^[0-9]+x[0-9]+_')

args=()
# Set the wallpaper via yin's IPC on every monitor (fall back to yin's
# default target if none are discovered yet, e.g. on a fresh cache).
if [ -z "$monitors" ]; then
  yinctl --img "$WALLPAPER" "${trans_args[@]}"
else
  while IFS= read -r m; do
    args+=("$m")
  done <<< "$monitors"
fi

for a in "${args[@]}"; do
  yinctl --img "$WALLPAPER" "${trans_args[@]}" --output "$a" &
done
wait

# Regenerate the colour scheme for this wallpaper. Use an absolute path so this
# works regardless of the caller's working directory (e.g. a Hyprland keybind).
# Videos ship a pre-baked matugen JSON (matugen can't sample a video frame);
# images without one derive their palette live from the file.
wp_file="${WALLPAPER##*/}"
wp_stem="${wp_file%%.*}"
colors_json="$HOME/.config/hypr/matugen-colors/$wp_stem.json"
if [ -f "$colors_json" ]; then
  matugen json "$colors_json"
elif [ -f "$WALLPAPER" ] && file --mime-type -b "$WALLPAPER" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^image/'; then
  matugen image "$WALLPAPER"
else
  echo "set-wallpaper: no matugen palette for '$wp_stem' and '$WALLPAPER' is not an image; skipping colours" >&2
fi


# Track current wallpaper for restarts
ln -sf "$WALLPAPER" ~/.cache/current-wallpaper
